title: Elastic overspill and throttled retry orchestration - PRD sketch
content:
Summary:
This is a working PRD sketch for a new operator-mode feature set: Elastic Overspill + Throttled Retry Orchestration (EOR). Goal: keep tenant traffic flowing with acceptable latency and cost when Dedicated pools hit saturation, while enforcing isolation contracts and minimizing noisy-neighbor blast radius.

Why we need it (problem statement):
- Dedicated customers buy predictable committed capacity but still experience microbursts and bursty tails. Hard failures (rejections, 429s) cause customer-facing errors and churn.
- Existing approaches (hard failover to hosted, blunt throttling, preemptive eviction) either degrade UX or violate isolation guarantees.
- We need a more graceful, observable, and economical way to: 1) accept overspill onto controlled execution paths, 2) retry at paced rates with backoff (throttled retry), and 3) optionally degrade fidelity (lower-cost model or quantized variant) automatically.

Product goals and non-goals:
- Goals:
  - Maintain soft latency SLOs for committed tenants during moderate saturation (SLOs defined per fidelity lane).
  - Reduce hard rejections by 50% in sustained microburst scenarios while preserving isolation for priority tenants.
  - Provide transparent billing and cost accounting for overspill traffic.
  - Give operators clear knobs: overspill window, retry policy, tenant confinement, priority weighting.
- Non-goals:
  - Not a replacement for contractual reserved capacity expansion.
  - Not intended to handle multi-hour sustained overloads without manual intervention.

Key concepts and terminology (working):
- Overspill lane: ephemeral execution capacity (could be hosted, opportunistic dedicated slack, or cheaper quantized nodes) that accepts traffic beyond a tenant's reserved baseline.
- Throttled retry: an orchestrated client-side/call-proxy retry scheme that spaces retries to respect SLO budgets and backpressure signals.
- Failforward: route to best-effort lower-fidelity model variant (e.g., quantized or distilled) instead of failing.
- Soft quarantine: temporary relegation of misbehaving request patterns to constrained lanes with stricter rate limits and additional telemetry.

User stories:
- As a platform engineer, I want a per-tenant overspill policy so that we can let small bursts through without impacting other customers.
- As an SRE, I want clear dashboards showing overspill consumption and cost delta so I can reason about billing and capacity tradeoffs.
- As a product owner for a committed tenant, I want to opt into failforward where lower-cost models are used before rejecting requests.

Success metrics (first 90 days after rollout):
- 50% drop in 429 rejections for bursts under 5 minutes for opt-in tenants.
- <10% increase in unit cost for overspill-enabled tenants (configurable cap).
- Number of soft-quarantine events per week tracked and trended (target: <5 for normal ops).
- Mean time to detect and reconcile a tenant overspill anomaly < 15 minutes.

High-level design options (tradeoffs):
1) Central overspill broker (control-plane): maintains global accounting of overspill capacity, issues tokens for overspill requests, enforces priority.
   - Pros: simpler billing and global fairness policies.
   - Cons: control-plane latency and single point of decisioning.
2) Distributed soft-handoff (edge/runtime): each node enforces local overspill lane using token-buckets and consults the control-plane asynchronously for reconciliation.
   - Pros: lower tail latency, resilient under control-plane degradation.
   - Cons: eventual consistency on accounting; need reconciliation job.
Proposal: hybrid pattern — edge token bucket + periodic reconciler with a lightweight central token coordinator.

Runtime behavior (flow):
- Detect: per-pool admission controller observes threshold breach (e.g., 95th percentile concurrency > X).
- Offer: controller signals eligible requests with an "overspill-allowed" header/token and marks metric.
- Route: router chooses lane: hosted-overspill, opportunistic-dedicated, or model-degrade lane based on tenant policy and real-time cost/latency signals.
- Retry: client proxy applies throttled retry policy (controlled jitter, max attempts, backoff window) and surfaces provenance in logs (overspill, failforward, retry-count).
- Reconcile: background job reconciles overspill ledger to apply billing adjustments and remediate token drift.

Isolation controls and fairness:
- Priority weights: tenants get a priority score used when overspill capacity is scarce.
- Hard isolation anchors: guaranteed minimal capacity (reservation) is never preempted by overspill consumers.
- Soft quarantine triggers: abnormal request rate patterns (sustained queueing, CPU hot loops, malformed workloads) get placed into quarantine lane for triage, with auto-heal timers.

Autoscaler integration:
- Autoscaler will be overspill-aware: overspill activity signals can be used as an early indicator to scale pool capacity when sustained (policy threshold > TTL).
- Tie to predictive autoscaling heuristics: if overspill consistently exceeds X% of pool baseline over Y minutes, trigger scale-up pipeline.

Observability and tooling:
- New metrics: overspill_tokens_issued, overspill_cost_delta, overspill_latency_p50/p95/p99, quarantine_events, failforward_rate, retry_backoff_effectiveness.
- Dashboards: per-tenant overspill heatmap, pool-wide overspill budget burn-down, and cost impact simulator.
- Logs: structured fields to link a request to overspill tokens, lane, and retry history; propagate in tracing.

Billing and UX surfaces:
- Option A: explicit overspill billing line item (metered per-token/minute); tenants see clear delta on invoices.
- Option B: overspill included up to a soft-cap for paid tiers; above cap charged.
- Product decision: default to Option A for transparency; provide per-customer opt-in blending for enterprise deals.

Rollout plan (staged):
1) Internal dogfood: enable on non-critical tenants and internal teams with observability and forced quotas.
2) Beta: invite 5 customers to opt-in with explicit billing preview.
3) Gradual rollout: open behind feature flag; default off for committed tenants.
4) GA: expose UI in Console with simple knobs (enable overspill, failforward preference, max cost delta).

Operational runbook (draft):
- On overspill storm: prioritize high-SLA tenants, throttle retries globally, enable emergency model-degrade lane if tail latency spikes.
- If token reconciliation drift > 5%: pause overspill issuance and run ledger repair job; notify billing.
- Quarantine review: product + SRE + solutions-eng weekly triage for quarantined tenant patterns.

Risks and open questions (brain dump):
- Cost unpredictability for customers who forget opt-in. Need clear signals/warnings in Console and alerting if spend approaches cap.
- Complexity in ledger reconciliation under network partitions.
- Potential privacy/security surface if overspill routes to hosted nodes — need data isolation opt-outs.
- How to set fair default priority weights across many tenants? Do we use commit size, recent spend, latency SLO, or a combination?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Spike: prototype edge token-bucket + reconciler (2 week spike) — estimate infra effort: 1 PM, 2 SRE, 2 infra engs.
- Safety: run small-scale chaos tests (node failover + overspill) during dogfood.
- Draft Console UX: simple toggle + cost cap slider + model-degrade checkbox. Ask Dana for a mock.
- Billing: work with finance to define SKU and invoice line description.

Open decisions required from Product Council:
- Default billing mode (Option A vs B).
- Whether hosted overspill nodes are allowed for customers with strict private deployment requirements.
- Priority weight formula baseline.

Bottom line: EOR is intended to reduce hard failures and improve customer experience during bursts while preserving the essential isolation guarantees of Dedicated. This doc is a sketch — next step is spike and a short RFC for the control-plane design.
